contract: The no-C-compiler job is expected to FAIL while this list is non-empty, and expected to fail ONLY for reasons on it. A failure whose reason is absent here is a regression, not progress. The list is the phase's schedule: it shrinks patch by patch, and the job becomes required when it empties -- by a patch that says so, never automatically.

scripts/phase25_musl_c_free_link.py builds the runtime crate for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, links a program that CALLS gust_tick through rust-lld with cc/gcc/clang/c++/g++/cc1/ld/ld.gold/ld.bfd all poisoned to exit 99, runs it, and requires exit 7 and no INTERP segment.

Patch 25.11 had measured 'musl + rust-lld + ld.lld flavor WORKS: static-pie, exit 7' but could not include the runtime archive, and said so: 'THE GATE IS NOT PROVABLE UNTIL THE RUNTIME STOPS BEING C'. 25.5, 25.6 and 25.10a finished that; PHASE21_RUNTIME_OBJECTS is empty and the archive is ar rcs over one Rust object.
The five glibc symbols this entry named -- __printf_chk, __fprintf_chk, __memcpy_chk, __isoc23_strtol, __stack_chk -- are absent from the musl archive (nm --undefined-only: 0 each).

MUTATION-TESTED: with nothing poisoned the guard refuses to certify ('the poisoned cc did not fire'); with the archive off the link path it fails 'unable to find library'. Baseline restores byte-identical.
cleared.what_this_does_not_claim: NOT that `make gust` is C-free on gnu. Patch 25.11 decided the user default stays the host target (O6) and that a gnu host with no C compiler ERRORS naming musl rather than silently switching (P10). 25.11 measured that no stock C-free link exists on gnu at all. This is the musl proof the phase always said it would be.

cleared.reason_when_recorded: rustc uses cc as its linker driver on *-linux-gnu, including for the musl self-contained target, so a C-free link needs -C linker=rust-lld explicitly.
cleared.cleared_by: Patch 25.12b, by configuring the linker the entry itself named
evidence: The entry's own reason ends '...so a C-free link needs -C linker=rust-lld explicitly.' That is exactly what clears it.

MEASURED, and it is NOT gnu-specific: a musl host (rust:alpine) with cc, gcc and clang shadowed off PATH fails with `error: linker `cc` not found` -- this entry's own observable_signature. rustc's DEFAULT driver is cc on every host, so no image swap clears it.

With RUSTFLAGS='-C linker=rust-lld -C linker-flavor=ld.lld' on that same musl host and still no C compiler: cargo build exits 0 and the binary RUNS. scripts/phase25_musl_c_free_link.py host-build asserts this, arming itself first by requiring the image show no cc.
MUTATION-TESTED: removing the RUSTFLAGS makes the guard fail, so it is the configuration being measured and not the image.
The companion arm proves the other half -- a program calling gust_tick links against the musl runtime archive through rust-lld with nine C drivers poisoned, runs, and is static-pie.
cleared.what_remains_a_workflow_change: The no-C falsifier job runs `make gust` on ubuntu-latest, a GNU host. Patch 25.11 measured that gnu has NO C-free link at all, and cargo builds build scripts for the HOST regardless of --target, so libm's build script reaches for cc there and nothing can be configured away. Flipping the job green needs a musl IMAGE as well as this configuration. That is a workflow change, not an expected failure: the barrier this entry names is gone.

cleared.reason_when_recorded: The Cranelift backend links its objects by spawning a C driver: compiler/experiments/cranelift/src/main.rs:16533 reads `env::var_os("CC").unwrap_or_else(|| "cc")`. Removing C COMPILATION from the tree does not remove C LINKING from the native route.
cleared.cleared_by: Patch 25.12b, by giving the backend the non-cc link step this entry asked for
evidence: The entry's cleared_by: 'an internal or non-cc link step for the native backend -- lld, or a linker invoked directly rather than through a C driver.' GUST_NATIVE_LINK_FLAVOR=rustc-lld is that step: rustc drives, rust-lld links, the target is musl, the result is static-pie.

VERIFIED END TO END, not by probe: with cc, gcc, clang, c++, g++, cc1, ld, ld.gold and ld.bfd all poisoned to exit 99, compiler/typechecker_resource_declaration_bridge_test_entry.gst compiles through the native backend, links, produces a 6MB artifact with ZERO INTERP segments, and RUNS with exit 0.

main.rs:16532 no longer has only `env::var_os("CC").unwrap_or("cc")`. Two request fields carry the flavour: link_via_rustc, because rustc reads bare positional paths as CRATE FILES so objects must go through -C link-arg; and trailing_linker_args, because rustc wants its crate file last.

I had called this intractable, twice, on the grounds that a direct rust-lld line must enumerate every std rlib the Gust runtime archive depends on. That is true of rust-lld invoked DIRECTLY and false of rustc, which computes the set itself. The assumption was never tested until it was.
cleared.default_unchanged: The C driver remains the default on the host target. Patch 25.11 decided the user default stays native (O6) and that a gnu host with no C compiler ERRORS naming musl rather than silently returning a static binary with a non-functional dlopen (P10). This adds a route; it switches no one.
